page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is configured with 2048.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, which provides 16.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided by 3800 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with the Passmark CPU score and extended instructions testing placing in the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is consistently strong across both cached small-block reads at 6746.43 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 334.29 GB/sec. Single-core performance, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics, falls within the average range. The server also exhibits strong capabilities in database operations, handling 113.64 million Redis SET operations per second, and static web serving throughput of 74.04 GB/sec.

Given its bare-metal architecture and massive memory footprint, this server offers high resource density for memory-intensive workloads, though it lacks GPU acceleration. The qualitative cost efficiency is aligned with enterprise-grade, high-capacity memory requirements where virtualized overhead must be avoided. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory analytics, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-bound scientific simulations.
